text.p: A merged Cie de Suez and Lyonnaise des Eaux will see growth from worldwide trends in urbanisation and privatisation, Lyonnaise chairman Jerome Monod said on Friday.

The new group will benefit from global trends towards "rapid urbanisation and the development of markets for environmental services, deregulation of public monopolies, privatisations and recourse to management contracts," he told reporters on the merger plan.
Suez and Lyonnaise earlier announced their merger to form a utilities group with annual sales of over 200 billion francs.

Asked if Lyonnaise had been forced into a merger by French archrival Cie Generale des Eaux, Monod said: "The problem for the new group we are forming between Suez and Lyonnaise is dictated by the evolution of global markets and global competition and not by purely French competition."
"Whoever thinks at the French level, I believe is making a mistake over the continent and the times in which we live," he said.
"It is not a question of growing for its own sake, but to have a financial strength, a human resources capability and the business necessary to play a leadership role on the global level," he said.
